standard_prerequisites.name: An etale localised map is faithfully flat, and a localisation of a finite type algebra over a Noetherian ring is Noetherian

core_obligations: Note that the localised map is faithfully flat and conclude that Noetherianness of the target local ring descends to the source (proof lines 10820-10825).
Conversely, assuming the source local ring Noetherian, use that the target local ring is a localisation of a finite type algebra over it to conclude that it is Noetherian (proof lines 10825-10827).
proof_roadmap: Descent along the faithfully flat localised map (proof lines 10820-10825).
Finite type and localisation for the converse (proof lines 10825-10828).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for an etale map and primes one over the other, the local ring of the source is Noetherian exactly when the local ring of the target is, and the proof is an 8-line argument with two short directions. One direction is descent of Noetherianness along the faithfully flat localised map, quoted from a statement of the Algebra chapter; the other uses that the localised target is a localisation of a finite type algebra over the localised source, and finite type algebras and their localisations over a Noetherian ring are Noetherian. The two directions are each a single step and both are displayed.
